name: Fastly
aliases: Fastly free account + Fast Forward OSS programme

card.summary: "10 Million Compute requests free" a month and "100 Million Compute vCPU milliseconds free" a month, with overage at USD 0.50 per million requests and USD 0....

free_tier.stated: "10 Million Compute requests free" a month and "100 Million Compute vCPU milliseconds free" a month, with overage at USD 0.50 per million requests and USD 0.05 per million vCPU milliseconds.

egress.terms: The pricing page lists CDN bandwidth per region with the first 100 GB per month free and a per-GB price above it; whether bytes served by Compute meter under that table is unverified: the table is headed 'Bandwidth (per month)' and is not labelled for Compute

record.interface_detail: REST API at api.fastly.com and the fastly CLI, documented at fastly.com/documentation/reference
record.tooling: the fastly CLI, which builds and deploys Compute packages through the Fastly API
record.chaining: 10 million requests a month at the edge with no idle cost, useful as a front for an IPv6-only origin or as a webhook receiver that triggers a paid-for-nothing job elsewhere.

limits.value: The free tier is metered in vCPU milliseconds, so 100 million vCPU-ms a month is about 27.8 vCPU-hours, and a Compute program cannot stay resident at all because the model is one request at a time.

record.limits_note: The free tier is metered in vCPU milliseconds, so 100 million vCPU-ms a month is about 27.8 vCPU-hours, and a Compute program cannot stay resident at all because the model is one request at a time.
record.binding_note: The free tier is metered in vCPU milliseconds, so 100 million vCPU-ms a month is about 27.8 vCPU-hours, and a Compute program cannot stay resident at all because the model is one request at a time.

identity_cost.detail: a card is required: the vendor's own announcement states the free developer accounts "require a valid credit card to help prevent abuse on the platform". The record does not state whether the card is charged or authorised for any amount, whether a hold is placed and for how long, whether a debit or prepaid card is accepted, or whether an email or phone is also required at signup

evidence.proved: Compute section: 0 to 10 million Compute requests free, 0 to 100 million Compute vCPU milliseconds free, quoted
"We provide a monthly free tier of services for many Network Services and Compute products", charged only above the limits, quoted
vendor update on the same page: the free tier is more generous now but "require a valid credit card to help prevent abuse on the platform"
a REST API covers the platform
evidence.quote: The Fastly API is a RESTful API that provides access to all the features available through the Fastly web interface.

evidence.proved: the pricing page lists 100 GB per month of free CDN bandwidth in every region
evidence.quote: | 0 - 100 GB | Free | Free | Free | Free | Free | Free | Free | Free | Free | Free |
The Fastly API is a RESTful API that provides access to all the features available through the Fastly web interface.
`fastly` is an [open-source](https://github.com/fastly/cli) command line tool for interacting with the [Fastly API](https://www.fastly.com/documentation/reference/api).

record.notes: The card requirement converts this from an anonymous free tier into a payment relationship, which is why identity_cost is card. Compute is WebAssembly, so a process that needs a shell, a kernel or a long-lived socket does not fit. 27.8 vCPU-hours a month is the number to compare against Deno's 10 and Cloudflare's CPU-time model.

card.summary: No byte quota - free CDN/edge services for eligible OSS projects and the nonprofits that support them. Scope set per applicant after review.

free_tier.stated: No byte quota - free CDN/edge services for eligible OSS projects and the nonprofits that support them. Scope set per applicant after review.

egress.terms: This is the egress: Fastly absorbs bandwidth for accepted projects. Origin still has to exist and be paid for elsewhere.

record.tooling: Fastly CDN/VCL, custom VCL or Compute@Edge; standard HTTP origin pull.
record.chaining: Use as the free front door over any of the qualifying origins (Hugging Face, Internet Archive, a university bucket). Turns a metered origin into an unmetered public read path.
record.limits_note: Google Form application; acceptance discretionary and reviewed by a human. Must be open-licensed, community-centred, 'built on trust'. No published SLA. Not a storage product at all.
record.reliability_note: Established programme (relaunched 2022) with real OSS members (PyPI historically). Risk is acceptance, not durability. Adds a third-party dependency in the read path.

evidence.proved: 'we extend free services to eligible open source projects and nonprofits that support them'; application is an embedded Google Form
'Fast Forward will offer free services to open source projects and the nonprofits that support them'

record.notes: No byte quota - free CDN/edge services for eligible OSS projects and the nonprofits that support them. Scope set per applicant after review.

free_tier.stated: 100 GB bandwidth and 100,000 requests per month

egress.terms: 100 GB/month per region, then USD 0.12 to 0.28/GB by region

record.chaining: composes with an origin and a domain, and the 100 GB is spent per region so a multi-region service spends it several ways.
record.reliability_note: the free band is metered per region

evidence.proved: '100 GB free' and '100,000 free' requests, with the per-region band table

record.notes: 100 GB a month is about 3.3 GB a day.

extras.transit_note: the CDN serves the origin's bytes from its edge

record.binding_note: the monthly byte allowance in egress.free_allowance is what runs out, and no kind in the six-value vocabulary names a byte volume over a period counted per account. per-ip-shaping is the closest, because it is the only kind that bounds a volume, and its subject here is the account rather than the caller's address
record.limits_note: the allowance is a byte volume over a period, which none of the six kinds names; the number is in egress.free_allowance and binding names per-ip-shaping as the nearest kind

record.provider: Fastly free account + Fast Forward OSS programme

free_tier.stated: Free account: 100 GB bandwidth/month free across all regions, 1M CDN requests/month, 5 domains, 100K purge requests. Above 100 GB: $0.12/GB EU/NA, $0.19/GB Asia/Australia, $0.28/GB Africa/India/South Korea. Fast Forward (OSS/nonprofit programme) has no published byte quota. 'we extend free services to eligible open source projects and nonprofits that support them', scope agreed after human review of a Google Form application.

egress.terms: 100 GB/mo free, then metered per region. Fast Forward absorbs bandwidth for accepted projects but is the only path to meaningful volume.

record.tooling: VCL / Compute@Edge; standard HTTP origin pull. Free accounts are self-serve at fastly.com/signup.

limits.value: review of a Google Form application

record.limits_note: per-object-cap: none. The binding limit is the 100 GB/month counter (and 1M requests). Fast Forward: discretionary human acceptance, no published SLA, and the previous '$50/month of free traffic' credit model was retired for new accounts created after 2025-10-28.
record.reliability_note: Bandwidth is metered per region with no pooling, so a geographically mixed audience burns the 100 GB fastest. Fast Forward is real (PyPI, Rust Foundation, PSF, Kubernetes, Mastodon, 100+ projects) and worth applying to if any dataset ships as a public OSS artefact.

evidence.proved: 'Bandwidth | 100 GB free | Billed per GB per Region per month'; per-region table 0-100 GB Free, 100 GB-10 TB $0.28 Africa / $0.19 Asia / $0.12 Europe / $0.12 North America
'we extend free services to eligible open source projects and nonprofits that support them'; application is an embedded Google Form; criteria 'Open … Community-centered … Built on trust'
'monthly free tier of services for many Network Services and Compute products, subject to certain limitations'; OSS programme contact [address removed]
